verbalization: The visible evidence suggests a potential relationship between the compound (1R,3R,4R,7R,9S,10R,13R,14R)-14-(hydroxymethyl)-5,5,9-trimethyltetracyclo[11.2.1.01,10.04,9]hexadecane-3,7,14-triol and the protein PITSLRE serine/threonine-protein kinase CDC2L1, through a series of intermediate targets. The compound is identified as a target of Npc133119, which in turn is a target of Natural resistance-associated macrophage protein 2. This chain of interactions implies that the compound may influence the activity of CDC2L1 via the Npc133119 and Natural resistance-associated macrophage protein 2 pathways. The mechanism is likely mediated through the interaction of the compound with Npc133119, which then modulates the activity of CDC2L1. The evidence supports a possible regulatory role of the compound in the kinase activity of CDC2L1, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be elucidated.
